issues.evidence: probe P13b_user_organizer_py_moved fail; A/organizer.py:20,33 skips any top-level file whose name equals the script basename
issues.summary: A user file named organizer.py in the target directory is silently never organized, even when the script lives elsewhere.
Minor style lint (long lines, percent formatting); move failures go to stderr only, not organizer.log (A/organizer.py:73).

issues.evidence: probe P13a_tmp_part_files_moved fail; B/organizer.py:14,51 TEMP_SUFFIXES {.part,.crdownload,.tmp,.download} skipped in both --once and --watch
issues.summary: Unrequested rule silently leaves .tmp/.part/.crdownload/.download files unorganized forever, even in --once mode.

issues.evidence: B/ contains only organizer.py; static/B-ruff.txt: 3 E501
issues.summary: No tests provided; minor long-line lint.

blinding_guess.why: A ships a unittest suite that maps one-to-one onto the stated requirements (stdlib-only, single file, skips, log), suggesting a spec-driven process.

notes: Both sides are functionally sound: --once/--watch, extension-based moves, organizer.log, hidden/subdir skips, collision-safe renaming, and stdlib-only were verified by black-box probes on both. Each fails exactly one probe due to an extra skip rule (A: files named organizer.py; B: temp/partial-download suffixes); B's rule affects more common file types and also applies in --once, so it was rated medium. B's watch mode adds a size-stability delay before moving, which is reasonable and did not break the watch probe. Bandit reported no issues for either side. Probes require python>=3.10 (run with python3.11); both programs also ran correctly under system python 3.9.
